# Yuku, a JavaScript/TypeScript Compiler Toolchain in Zig

> Yuku is a JavaScript and TypeScript compiler toolchain written in Zig.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](https://yuku.fyi/): Yuku is a JavaScript and TypeScript compiler toolchain written in Zig.
- [Parser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/): Parse JavaScript, TypeScript, and JSX into a tree.
- [AST](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/): The tree the parser produces, and how to read, build, and edit it.
- [Semantic Analysis](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/): Scopes, symbols, resolved references, early errors, and module records for a parsed tree.
- [Traverse](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/): Walk and transform a tree with typed visitor hooks.
- [Codegen](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/): Print a tree back to JavaScript or TypeScript, with type stripping, minification, and source maps.
- [Testing](https://yuku.fyi/testing/): How Yuku is tested.
- [Security](https://yuku.fyi/security/): How to report a vulnerability in Yuku, and the security practices behind the toolchain and its releases.
- [JavaScript](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/packages/yuku#readme): Use Yuku from JavaScript and TypeScript with the yuku package.
- [Dialects](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/src/parser/dialect#readme): Add your own syntax to JavaScript, TypeScript, and JSX.

## Resources
